skill.title: Apply Theorem 9: Parallelogram: opposite sides and opposite angles equal
skill.output: unknown found, justified by citing Theorem 9

legend.1: the given 115° angle, copied to its opposite angle
legend.2: the unknown angle α or β

steps.ask: α is opposite the angle SPQ. What do opposite angles of a parallelogram have in common?
steps.title: Find α

lines.text: Opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal, so $\hl{2}{\alpha}$ equals $\hl{1}{|\angle SPQ|}$.

steps.ask: β and the angle SPQ share a side. What do adjacent angles of a parallelogram add to?
steps.title: Find β

lines.text: Adjacent angles of a parallelogram add to $\hl{3}{180^\circ}$.

lesson.note: The angles are now expressions in x and y, so each rule gives an equation and you solve them one after the other. The two rules are the same as in problem 1.

steps.ask: (2x − 30)° is opposite the 100° angle. What do opposite angles of a parallelogram tell you?
steps.title: Opposite angles are equal: find x

lines.text: $(2\hl{2}{x}-30)^\circ$ is opposite the $\hl{1}{100^\circ}$ angle, so they are equal.

steps.ask: (x + 3y)° and 100° are next to each other on one side. What do adjacent angles add to, and what does that give you for x + 3y?
steps.title: Adjacent angles sum to 180°

lines.text: $(\hl{2}{x}+3\hl{2}{y})^\circ$ and $\hl{1}{100^\circ}$ are adjacent angles, so they add to $\hl{3}{180^\circ}$.

steps.ask: Which side is equal and parallel to [FB]? How far, and in which direction, is T from Q?

lines.text: In $FBQT$, the side $[TQ]$ is parallel and equal to $\hl{1}{[FB]}$. $\hl{1}{[FB]}$ goes straight up 5 units, so $\hl{2}{T}$ is 5 units directly below $Q$.
